exercise2.prompt: A list of fruits, a tuple of coordinates, {"city": "New York"}, and the set {1, 2, 2, 3}, each labelled in a comment

cases.describe: a comment naming the type above each of the four structures

exercise2.hint: Write each structure with the punctuation that belongs to it, then let the output tell you what you got. The set is the interesting one: give it 1, 2, 2, 3 and see how many values come back.

questions.prompt: Which structure refuses to hold the same value twice?
questions.explain: A set stores unique values, so {1, 2, 2, 3} holds three things, not four. That is what makes it the tool for removing duplicates.

questions.prompt: Match each piece of Python to the structure it creates.
questions.explain: The punctuation is the whole difference. Curly braces mean a dictionary when the values are written as key: value, and a set when they are not.

questions.prompt: Which of these can be changed after they are created?
questions.explain: Only the tuple is immutable. Once it exists you can read from it, but nothing can be added, removed or replaced.

questions.prompt: To look a value up by a label rather than by a position, you reach for a ___.
questions.explain: A list is indexed by position and a dictionary by key. Which one you want depends on how you already know the thing you are looking for.
The repeat is dropped as the set is built, so the set never contains it. It is not an error and nothing warns you about it.
